simple.meaning: עִלָּה (ʻillâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a pretext (as arising artificially).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 6:5. Its contexts include Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עִלָּה (H5931).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עִלָּה (ʻillâh) / H5931 is traced through Daniel 6:5, Daniel 6:6 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5931. illah עִלָּה noun feminine matter, affair, occasion (Syriac , see Biblical Hebrew I. עלל ); — absolute ׳ע Dan 6:5 (twice in verse); 6:6 ( = ground of accusation).
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) feminine from a root corresponding to 5927 ;
